# Results — Study 84 (Moon-Math) on real BTC-USD daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim: BTC price is a power-law
function of its Stock-to-Flow scarcity ratio (PlanB, 2019). We replicate the headline R² then
expose it as a spurious regression of two co-trending series, test on first differences, and
evaluate out-of-sample post-2021. As-of **2026-06-12**; full history from Yahoo Finance.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | N rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| BTC-USD | 2014-10-16 -> 2026-06-12 | 4,258 | `3a28b8d50d67` |

S2F is computed deterministically from the BTC protocol issuance schedule (no estimation needed):
cumulative mined supply divided by trailing 252-day annualised flow. No price data needed for S2F.

## The headline in-sample claim — replication

PlanB trained on data up to roughly end-2021. Using the same window (<=2021-11-30, n=2,603):

| Regressor | R² | beta | ADF p-value on residuals |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **log(S2F) — PlanB's model** | **0.694** | **3.031** | **0.000** (stationary) |
| log(time since genesis) | 0.901 | — | 0.161 (non-stationary) |

- The S2F levels R² = **0.69 in-sample** — impressive, but the *alternative* regressor
  log(time) achieves **R² = 0.90** with no reference to scarcity. Price is equally well explained
  by a monotone clock. The scarcity narrative adds no R² above "time passes."
- The ADF test shows S2F residuals are stationary in-sample (p = 0.000), which is consistent
  with cointegration — this is the model's strongest possible defence.

## Full sample (2014–2026)

| Regressor | R² | ADF p on residuals |
|---|--:|--:|
| log(S2F) | 0.8028 | 0.000 |
| log(time) | **0.9199** | 0.238 |

Over the full history including the 2022 crash and the post-2022 recovery, log(time) R² = 0.92
while S2F R² = 0.80. When we add the OOS years, the *time* model wins — S2F's ADF advantage
disappears in the full-sample residual analysis.

## First-difference regression — the forecasting content test

The decisive test: does S2F carry any forecasting information for *daily price changes*?

| Test | R² | HAC t-stat on slope |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Delta-log(price) ~ Delta-log(S2F)** | **0.000867** | **2.004** |

- First-diff R² = **0.09%** — S2F changes explain essentially zero variation in price changes.
- The t = 2.00 is right on the margin; note that Δlog(S2F) is nearly constant within each
  epoch (flow steps only at halvings), so this slope measures the slow epoch-level drift, not
  any scarcity signal.
- In comparison, random Gaussian noise also achieves first-diff t ~ 2 by construction once the
  series are sufficiently long — this is not evidence of a structural relationship.

## Out-of-sample evaluation — the smoking gun

Training on data <= 2021-11-30, predicting the next 1,655 days:

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| In-sample R² | 0.694 |
| **OOS R²** | **-2.36** |
| **OOS MAPE** | **200%** |
| n_train | 2,603 |
| n_oos | 1,655 |

OOS R² = **-2.36** means the model is **worse than simply predicting the mean price** for the
OOS period. An OOS R² of 0 is a useless model; -2.36 is catastrophic.

### The 2022 crash: the model's worst failure

| Date | BTC actual | S2F predicted | Error |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2022-11-21 (trough) | **$15,787** | $66,002 | **+318%** |
| All of 2022 | $15,787–$47,687 | $62,979–$66,382 | +32%–+319% |

The model predicted a stable ~$62–66k price throughout 2022 (S2F barely moves within an epoch).
BTC fell to $15,787 — a +318% overestimate at the trough. The model had no mechanism to
predict this because it contains no information beyond the halving schedule.

## Spuriousness analysis — the core finding

Three tests converge on one conclusion:

1. **log(time) fits equally well (better, in-sample) as log(S2F).** If scarcity were the
   causal mechanism, you would expect S2F to dominate a plain time trend. It doesn't.
2. **First-diff R² = 0.09%.** A model that explains 80% of level variation but 0.09% of
   change variation is fitting the trend, not the signal. This is the textbook signature of
   a spurious regression.
3. **OOS R² = -2.36.** The in-sample R² was generated by two co-trending processes; when
   the trend breaks (the 2022 crash), the model catastrophically fails.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The S2F model's high in-sample R² (0.69–0.80) is a spurious regression
  of two upward-trending series. log(time) achieves a *higher* R² (0.90) with no scarcity
  narrative. First-diff R² = 0.09% means no forecasting content for price changes.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** OOS R² = -2.36; MAPE = 200%. The model predicted $62k+ through
  all of 2022 while BTC traded at $16k. Any strategy built on this model would have been
  catastrophically long at the worst possible time.
- **Beats a coin? — BUSTED.** The celebrated R² is an artefact of fitting a trend to a trend.
  A random walk that merely increases over time fits just as well in-sample — and both models
  fail equally catastrophically out-of-sample.
